title: Surge slicing & kernel coordination stabilization for asymmetric tokens/sec drop
creator: Aisha Kumar
description:
Summary: Multiple customers across Hosted, Dedicated and Private deployments reported a sudden asymmetric drop in tokens/sec and elevated TTFT p95 starting 2026-03-09 22:00 UTC. Impact was worst for mixed-length prompt workloads (short priming + long generation) and for customer-private clusters with pinned quantized variants.

Observed behavior: Token emission rate collapsed by ~40-60% for affected requests, first-token latency increased median ~120ms and p95 up to several seconds. GPU utilization dropped despite high queue lengths; scheduler logs show higher-than-usual slice preemption and a surge of small microbatches routed to a fallback kernel. KV cache hit-rate remained stable, but per-request kernel selection telemetry spiked in "fallback" path.

Root-cause hypothesis: A coordination race between the slice-allocator (which slices long contexts into multi-stage microbatches) and our kernel-selection heuristic resulted in the allocator assigning slices that the kernel selector considered "incompatible" with the high-throughput int8 path for that model variation. That triggered frequent kernel fallback/evictions, kernel reinitialization overhead, and inefficient multiplexing windows, producing per-request token-rate collapse (especially on multi-tenant fanout). The failure surface is amplified by aggressive warm-start heuristics and by private clusters that pin quantized artifacts without fallback variants.

Immediate mitigations applied (rolled 2026-03-10):
- Deployed a control-plane flag to prefer kernel affinity for in-flight models (kernel pinning) to avoid hot-swapping when slice patterns are ambiguous. Canary across 1% Hosted traffic.
- Enabled temporary request hedging for long-generation requests to hedged-compatible variant (only for Dedicated), reducing customer visible TTFT spikes.
- Disabled aggressive slice preemption and extended microbatch coalescing timeout from 4ms to 12ms to reduce churn.
- Pushed a coordination fix that serializes kernel-init per worker to prevent concurrent reinitializations.

Current status: Canary telemetry shows tokens/sec recovery to ~90% of baseline for canary cohort on Hosted. Dedicated hedging reduced customer-facing p95 by ~35% on observed tenants. Private clusters: patch packaged as v1.21.2 runtime build and staged for customer opt-in upgrade; one enterprise customer accepted the package and saw full recovery after upgrade.

Rollout plan:
1) Continue 1% Hosted canary for 24h, monitor kernel_mismatch_rate, tokens/sec p50/p95, queue depth, GPU load.
2) Gradual ramp to 10% then 50% Hosted over 48h if no regressions.
3) For Dedicated, apply hedging + kernel affinity change via hotpatch; network team to validate no added tail latency for isolated tenants.
4) For Private: provide runtime-1.21.2 package with opt-in instructions and a one-click console-assisted upgrade for managed Private customers; recommend immediate upgrade for enterprise customers impacted.

Tests & Acceptance Criteria:
- tokens/sec p50 within 10% of baseline and p95 reduction vs current incident baseline by at least 30% across representative prompt sets.
- kernel_mismatch_rate < 0.5% across canary cohort.
- No increase in soft OOMs or kernel-init error rate.

Postmortem items (next 2 sprints):
- Add kernel_mismatch_rate and per-model kernel-affinity signal to per-route console dashboards.
- Harden kernel-selection unit tests to cover slice-boundary cases and quantized variant pinning.
- Add automated alert that correlates token/sec collapse with kernel-init spikes and queue length.
- Design an autoscale-safe hedging policy that can be enabled per-customer.
